31: The power of Axon 2
32: For most of our history, AppLovin focused primarily on games. That was not a strategic limitation; it was a choice to stay focused while we built our technical capabilities. We became experts in helping game developers grow their businesses, and that focus, paired with technology, helped us become the largest user acquisition channel for mobile gaming in the world.
33: However, accurately valuing consumers playing games for offers that aren’t games requires predicting an even more complex chain of behaviors. We have to predict ad engagement, click-through rates, app or site engagement, conversion likelihood, payment probability, purchase size, and repeat behavior over time outside of the contextual relevancy of games. Advertisers require AppLovin to give them a return. If they spend $1,000, they must generate meaningfully more than $1,000 in lifetime value. Even small inaccuracies in prediction break the economics.
34: In April 2023, we rolled out our AI model, Axon 2. While Axon 1 performed this task well for gaming, Axon 2 significantly expanded our model capacity in gaming and unlocked every other major advertiser category. These models now predict expected value distributions many days into the future with enough precision to support real-time capital allocation across e-commerce, subscription services, and other verticals.

54: How does Axon AI work?
55: Businesses of all sizes use AppLovin Ads to automate, optimize, and manage their marketing efforts.
56: Advertisers set specific return goals for their advertising campaigns.
57: Axon AI’s predictive algorithms then evaluate potential impressions with the goals of meeting advertisers’ return on advertising spend targets and other marketing objectives and finding the users most likely to download or otherwise engage with their product(s).
58: AppLovin bids on impressions based on Axon AI’s determination of the value of the impression to the particular advertiser.
59: AppLovin earns revenues based on the value we drive for advertisers.  Our performance-based advertising model therefore demands that ads served by us lead to genuine, high-intent engagement, ensuring our campaigns deliver meaningful, measurable results for advertisers.
60: What data does Axon AI use?
61: Complex AI models, like Axon AI, train and optimize on a continual basis using an assortment of data.  Our models use device and network information and other information we have collected, or our partners share, about users’ engagement with applications, ads, and other digital properties, as described in our
62: Privacy Policy
63: and
64: How AppLovin Shows You Ads
65: page.  In addition, our models use win or loss notifications from our in-app bidding and monetization solution known as AppLovin Max, which all bidders receive depending on whether the bidder won or lost a particular impression.  Our models also use advertisers’ own data about their users if they choose to share that data with us.
66: We do not collect or seek to elicit—and our models do not ingest—users’ “sensitive personal information” (such as social security numbers, precise geolocation, racial and ethnic characteristics, religious or philosophical beliefs, or the contents of messages) or protected characteristics (such as age and gender).  In addition, we do not collect or seek to elicit—and our models do not ingest—other bidders’ bid information or other bidders’ user data.  We also explicitly prohibit partners from initializing our technologies in connection with “children” or otherwise providing us with children’s data, and we prohibit apps exclusively designed for and/or exclusively directed to children on our platform.
67: For more information, please review our
68: Privacy Policy
69: and
70: How AppLovin Shows You Ads
71: page.
72: How does Axon AI continue to improve?
73: On an ongoing basis, Axon AI’s models experience compounding improvements through self-learning, continuing data ingestion, and engineering oversight and enhancements.  As more advertisers use our performance-based advertising solutions, the models improve through additional data and better insights (per the collection described above), which then further enhances the efficiency and effectiveness of AppLovin Ads.

21: Earlier this year, we launched
22: Prospecting Campaigns
23: , a campaign type for e-commerce advertisers that optimizes for purchases from people who have never bought from you before. Advertisers responded quickly, with many seeing meaningful lifts in new customer ROAS and broad adoption across the platform. However, some advertisers asked a natural next question:
24: what if I want to go even further and reach people who have never visited my site at all?
25: Today, we're addressing that question with Discovery Campaigns.
26: What Discovery Campaigns do differently
27: Where Prospecting Campaigns focus on converting visitors who haven't purchased yet, Discovery Campaigns go even further: optimizing for purchases from people who have never interacted with your brand in any way. No site visit. No browse. No add to cart. Discovery is built to introduce entirely new audiences to your brand and convert them.
28: AI optimizes. You choose what matters.
29: At Axon, we believe AI should do what it does best: optimize toward a clearly defined goal. Our models are relentless at finding the right person, at the right time, with the right ad, doing so at a scale no manual process can match.
30: But defining the goal is a business decision, not an algorithmic one.
31: Different advertisers grow in different ways. A subscription brand may prioritize first-time purchasers. A marketplace may focus on reaching entirely new visitors. Another business may want to maximize total conversions regardless of customer status.
32: There is no single “correct” objective. That is why we build campaign types around distinct definitions of success. Universal optimizes for total conversion performance. Prospecting focuses on new purchasers. Discovery goes one step further by optimizing for purchases from people who have never interacted with your brand at all.
33: You decide what growth means for your business. We ensure the system pursues it as efficiently as possible.
34: Getting started
35: If you’re already running Prospecting Campaigns, you’re already set up. Discovery is built on the same foundation and uses the same historical purchase data. Simply select Discovery in Axon Ads Manager to launch a campaign that reaches entirely new audiences.
36: If you’re not yet running Prospecting, share your historical purchase data in Ads Manager to get started. Shopify Shops are already covered through the app integration. Axon AI handles the rest.

14: How AppLovin Ad Review works
15: AppLovin Ad Review runs only on impressions MAX mediates, and only after a publisher turns it on in the MAX dashboard. The data is used to moderate ads and is aggregated for reporting; user-level detail exists today only so a publisher can trace a specific bad ad and block it. We do not build user or device profiles from it, and we do not feed it into Axon or any other AppLovin model. There is no scenario where we take another network's ad output and train our models on it. Even so, we are removing the user-level detail entirely. Catching a bad ad does not require it, and we would rather hold Ad Review to the standard we think every ad quality tool should meet.

15: D28 IAP ROAS
16: earlier this year, Unity Vector is now expanding to support two new campaign types: D28 Ad Revenue ROAS campaigns and D28 Hybrid ROAS campaigns.
17: These new additions extend D28 optimization to advertisers monetizing through ads or a mix of ads and in-app purchases, making it easier to acquire users whose value builds over time through ad engagement, purchases, or both.
18: With this launch, Unity Vector now offers a complete D28 ROAS suite across the major mobile game monetization models: IAP, Ad Revenue , and Hybrid (IAP + Ad Revenue)
19: What’s New
20: D28 Ad Revenue ROAS
21: D28 Ad Revenue ROAS is designed for games where ad revenue is the primary monetization stream.
22: Advertisers set a D28 ROAS target by country, and Unity Vector predicts each user’s likely ad revenue over 28 days, dynamically adjusting bids to optimize toward that target.
23: This campaign type is especially useful for games where:
24: ad engagement builds over time
25: retention is a key driver of monetization
26: a meaningful share of ad revenue happens beyond the first week
27: Based on Closed Beta results, D28 Ad Revenue ROAS delivers significantly higher retention and ARPU by leveraging Vector’s deep-funnel learnings.¹
28: 90% showed higher D28 retention vs D7, with a median uplift of +62%
29: 67% showed higher D28 total ARPU vs D7, with a median uplift of +68%
30: D28 Hybrid ROAS
31: D28 Hybrid ROAS is designed for games where both in-app purchases and ad revenue contribute meaningfully to user value.
32: Instead of optimizing separately for early IAP or early ad engagement, Hybrid D28 ROAS helps advertisers optimize toward a combined 28-day revenue signal. This makes it easier to acquire users whose total value would be underrepresented in a shorter or single-stream optimization window.
33: Based on Closed Beta results, D28 Hybrid ROAS delivers significantly higher retention and ARPU by leveraging Vector’s deep-funnel learnings.¹

38: D0 and D7 find users who monetize early. D28 is designed to complement it by helping advertisers reach users whose value builds beyond the first week. These strategies work best together, not as replacements for one another.

36: ## Learning phase best practices
37: 
38: The following best practices are specific to the [Learning phase](/grow/acquire/campaigns/roas/intro-to-roas-campaigns.md#learning-phase) of your ROAS campaign.
39: 
40: ### Collect unattributed postbacks from the Unity SDK
41: 
42: To accelerate your campaign's learning phase, use the Unity SDK to collect additional SDK data and ensure that you send Unity the corresponding post-install event’s [unattributed](/grow/acquire/partner-integration/attribution/introduction.md#attribution-types)  postbacks for at least two weeks before you create your new ROAS campaign. This data won’t be counted as part of the learning threshold, but helps to train the machine learning models that enable optimization. When you supply unattributed postbacks and SDK data before campaign launch, it can improve initial optimization predictions and help shorten the Learning phase.
43: 
44: ### Avoid setup changes during the Learning phase
45: 
46: While your campaign is in the Learning phase, avoid making changes to your campaigns settings, such as budgets or targeting parameters. Performance fluctuations are normal during this phase. Making changes during the Learning phase can disrupt the machine learning process and extend the Learning phase. After your campaign reaches **Live** status, you can optimize your settings for better performance.
47: 
48: ### Adjust ROAS goal if install volume is too low
49: 
50: While you should generally avoid setup changes during the Learning phase, you might need to adjust your ROAS goal if your campaign can't reach the [required install threshold](/grow/acquire/campaigns/roas/intro-to-roas-campaigns.md#learning-phase-thresholds). If your campaign has been in the Learning phase for an extended period without meeting the install requirement, lower your ROAS goal. This allows the system to place higher CPI bids and acquire more users, helping your campaign exit the Learning phase.
51: 
52: ### Focus on United States and Tier 1 countries during the Learning phase
53: 
54: During the learning phase, the recommended best practice is to launch with US or multiple top performing Tier 1 or Tier 2 countries. Tier 3 countries typically have lower user density and monetization rates, which can make it difficult to collect sufficient data during the Learning phase. This is especially true for IAP and Hybrid campaigns, which require payer data.
55: 
56: ## MMP integration best practices
57: 
58: The following best practices are specific to your preferred Mobile Measurement Partner (MMP) [integration](/grow/acquire/partner-integration.md) setup.
59: 
60: ### Send install data from all sources
61: 
62: When you share install data with Unity, ensure that you include data from your entire user base, including attributed, unattributed, and organic installs. Refer to the [Introduction to Attribution](/grow/acquire/partner-integration/attribution/introduction.md#attribution-types) for definitions of each attribution type.
63: 
64: ### Share both values and revenue for Purchase and Ad Revenue events
65: 
66: When you share Purchase or Ad revenue event data with Unity, share both values and revenue for each event. Sharing this complete data improves Unity's User Acquisition models and can improve campaign performance.
67: 
68: ### Set postback windows to lifetime if applicable
69: 
70: If your MMP supports lifetime postback windows, always set the window to lifetime. Otherwise, set your postback window to the maximum length. Setting your postback window to lifetime allows your campaign to learn from your app's entire install history and can improve campaign performance.

92:

94:

Your campaign might not achieve its ROAS goal during this phase, but performance typically improves when the campaign reaches Live status.

208: How Unity’s D28 IAP ROAS optimizer prevents D7 cannibalization
209: The question remains that if both campaign types bid on impressions in the same inventory, won’t they compete against each other and drive up costs?
210: Unity's analysis of D28 converters reveals that only 38%* of users who convert with in-app purchases by D28 spend in the first week. In other words, roughly two-thirds of high-value D28 spenders showed no early IAP conversion signals whatsoever.
211: These aren’t players who nearly converted on D7 but needed a few more days. They’re a different player cohort with different motivations, engagement patterns, and conversion triggers.
212: This is where Unity Vector's support is vital. Traditional optimization models can only see what happens after a user installs: Did they convert? How much did they spend? Unity Vector enables Unity IAP ROAS optimizers to see something more.
213: Because Unity powers both game creation and user growth, Unity Vector has unique visibility into player behavior and patterns.
214: Unity Vector combines holistic player and game intelligence to understand why certain players match with certain games, and when they're likely to convert. It uses both attributed data and unattributed data, like cross-game behavioral patterns and aggregate cohort insights, to distinguish between these player types at the moment of bid decision.
215: The future of ROAS optimization with Unity Vector
216: When UA efficiency increasingly plays a large role in which games succeed and which fail, leaving only 38% of IAP converters addressed isn't viable. And without the early converters of D7 campaigns, optimizers have less signals and businesses have less to invest in their late-game campaigns.
217: Both are necessary. And with Unity Vector powering both optimization windows, these Unity Ads campaign types can deliver better results as the model learns from Unity's place at the intersection of game creation and growth.
218: The architectural decision to optimize for holistic player and game intelligence means Unity Vector's optimization capabilities improve alongside games as they evolve and player behaviors shift - allowing Unity Vector to provide later LTV predictions as the market demands increasingly longer optimization windows. Ultimately, this ensures Unity is able to help creators build games that players love to play, and turn those games into profitable, sustainable businesses.

14: As the controller of your Developer Data, it’s your responsibility to respect end-user consent as is applicable to your business. Generally, this means you must present your users with appropriate opportunities to affirm or reject the various ways in which you intend to use their personal data.
15: 
16: To help you fulfill this responsibility, Unity has introduced the End-User Consent Mode: a developer-friendly way to manage user consent dynamically across supported Unity services.
17: 
18: Consent Mode allows end users to express their desired intent when making a particular consent decision. As a result, Unity products and services will be able to understand end-user consent relative to a particular use case – as opposed to service level Collect/Don’t Collect APIs that may unnecessarily suppress the value of the service to developers.
19: 
20: Consent Mode is fully integrated with the Developer Data framework and consolidates end-user consent management for all Unity products and services that operate using Developer Data. It works by allowing you to declare default consent states for your users and to maintain changes to their consent states in near real time along the following dimensions:
21: 
22: * `analytics_intent` 
23:   Controls whether Developer Data may be used in analytics and analytics-derived use cases that involve user-level identifiers.
24: 
25: * `ads_intent` 
26:   Controls whether Developer Data may be used in personalized advertising use cases and the collection of ads-specific device identifiers.
27: 
28: Each signal supports two values:
29: 
30: * `granted`: Unity will proceed with data collection and will use the data from the consenting user in accordance with the customer’s Developer Data usage settings.
31: * `denied`: Unity will suppress purpose-specific identifier collection for the unconsenting user, and may, where applicable, limit the collection of data events which are specific to applicable intent. Unity will act in accordance with the customer’s Developer Data usage settings, however, personal data from unconsented users will be filtered-out as indicated by the user.
32: 
33: Consent Mode is a core component of Unity’s Developer Data framework and applies specifically to your use of Developer Data pursuant to framework controls. Obtaining the proper consent from your end users is often critical. Consent Mode helps you align with privacy regulations and user expectations while maintaining transparency and control over how Developer Data is used across Unity products and services.
34: 
35: If no default end-user consent is configured via Consent Mode, Unity assumes that you’ve chosen to manage those states using another method, such as a developer-controlled implementation or service-specific consent APIs. In the event no end-user consent state is knowable or available, Unity interprets the lack of signal as if the set values were the following:
36:

38: * `ads_intent = denied`

excerpt:
20: We spend a lot of time talking to advertisers about measurement. Not because measurement is the most exciting topic in performance marketing, but because it's where confusion lives. And confusion, more than budget, more than creative, is usually what holds a brand back from getting the most out of a channel.
21: The conversations tend to go one of two ways. Either an advertiser comes to us saying AppLovin looks strong in-platform, but their third-party tool doesn't see it. Or they come in saying their MMM is actually attributing more to AppLovin than the platform itself reports. Both end up in the same place. The disagreement between those numbers is not telling you who is right. It is telling you what each model was built to see.
22: Stop waiting for one number to tell the whole story
23: Here is a simple way to think about it. A customer sees an AppLovin ad while playing a mobile game on a Tuesday afternoon. They don't click. Three days later, they search for the brand on Google, land on the site, and buy. On Friday, their roommate, reached by the same campaign, buys on Amazon without ever touching the DTC site.
24: Today, AppLovin's in-platform report sees neither of those conversions. Click-based attribution requires a click, and none happened. Your MTA tool picks up the Google search and gives it credit, maybe with a partial assist somewhere upstream. Your MMM may pick up that AppLovin spend correlates with a broader lift in demand, including the Amazon sale. Your post-purchase survey captures neither customer because they were never prompted. An incrementality test, run well, is the only instrument that would tell you with statistical confidence how many of those conversions genuinely would not have happened without the campaign.
25: None of those answers is wrong. They are just not measuring the same thing.
26: The advertiser who uses all of them to triangulate is in a much better position than the one waiting for a single source of truth that doesn't exist.
27: Half of what AppLovin drives never shows up in the dashboard
28: Fospha, which measures AppLovin across a growing cohort of ecommerce brands, has found that last-click and MTA models are significantly underreporting AppLovin's contribution, because the channel operates at a discovery layer those tools aren't built to see.
29: Source:
30: Fospha's AppLovin Playbook
31: Prescient's MMM benchmark series adds another layer:
32: Across our AppLovin cohort, roughly 50% of modeled value comes through halo, higher than Meta (~42%) or Google (~40%), and nearly half of that halo lands on Amazon. For brands with a heavy Amazon presence, the story is even stronger: halo climbs to ~60% of modeled value. The hypothesis makes sense: AppLovin is reaching high-intent users in mobile environments who convert later on Amazon, the channel they already trust for purchasing.
33: Will Holtz, Prescient COO & CFO
34: Both partners are pointing at the same thing. AppLovin's in-platform reporting is conservative, and its contribution is showing up well beyond what last-click captures.
35: AppLovin's impact is growing faster than its own reporting shows
36: We have now worked through a growing body of incrementality tests on AppLovin over the past 17 months since the first incrementality test came in. A few things stand out.
37: Tests have gotten better built over time. Advertisers have come to understand the mechanics now - what a holdout is doing, why test duration and geo balance matter, what a clean result actually requires. And because we review most designs before they launch, fewer tests go live underpowered or with a geo split that was never going to balance. None of that shows up as a single headline number. It shows up as results a brand can feel reasonably confident in and act on, instead of results we have to hedge.
38: The platform picture is also changing in ways that matter here. The incremental factor we observe, a brand's iROAS measured by a geo holdout experiment relative to its AppLovin in-platform reported ROAS, has more than doubled over the past year. In-platform reporting currently captures click-through attribution only and that gap between what the platform reports and what a controlled experiment reveals has been consistent with the third-party signals above: a meaningful share of what AppLovin drives isn't visible in its own reporting.
39: Not ready to test yet is not a reason to stop optimizing
40: The brands with the most consistent results understand that an incrementality test is a moment-in-time experiment with real constraints. Holdout size, budget level, test duration, geo composition, campaign stability - all of these interact.
41: A few of these we hold firm on: campaigns need to be out of the learning phase and delivering steadily before a test starts, holdouts are typically sized at 20-50% of the geo footprint, and we design every test to a minimum of 90% statistical power.

40: Media & creative
41: Media and creative feel like the easiest functions to integrate inside of a brand. Media needs assets to run in channels; creative needs performance data to produce better concepts. Yet at too many brands, these teams operate in parallel without integrated workflows.
42: This disconnect is especially costly on algorithmically driven platforms like AppLovin, where little to no manual targeting exists by design. Our models match the right user to the right ad relative to the conversion event the brand wants to achieve.
43: Media buyers still want to ensure they’re reaching new and diverse audiences and that their reach is expanding over time. On AppLovin Ads, creative is the primary lever to do this.
44: We encourage creative teams on our platform to think like media buyers. They control the targeting more than the media team does. Want to reach women? Make ads for women. Want to reach millennials? Make content that resonates with them. The model will find the right audience for whatever the creative team produces.
45: Breaking down the walls
46: None of these silos are unique to AppLovin. They exist across every marketing channel. But because AppLovin Ads is algorithmically driven and performance-based, the cost of these organizational gaps shows up faster and more visibly in the data.
